action_criteria.expected_evidence: Mild age-appropriate atrophy and punctate small-vessel white matter foci; no basal ganglia lacune, no ventriculomegaly; normal basal ganglia and midbrain signal and morphology; no mass or hemorrhage
action_criteria.label: Brain MRI to exclude a structural, vascular or atypical-parkinsonism cause
action_criteria.rationale: PD is a clinical diagnosis; MRI is normal in PD and excludes vascular lesions, NPH, mass and the midbrain, pontine and putaminal signs of PSP and MSA [Postuma_2015]

action_criteria.expected_evidence: UPSIT 22/40, severe microsmia: olfactory loss on a validated test
action_criteria.label: Consider a validated smell identification test for the reported smell loss
action_criteria.rationale: Self-reported or bedside smell loss is not an MDS supportive criterion; olfactory loss on a validated test for age and sex is, and with no red flag it turns clinically probable into clinically established PD [Postuma_2015]

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No dopamine receptor blocker; the alpha-blocker and the calcium-channel blocker flagged for standing blood pressure during titration
action_criteria.label: Review the medication list before starting dopaminergic treatment
action_criteria.rationale: No dopamine-blocking drug is on his list, but tamsulosin and amlodipine add to orthostatic falls once levodopa is started [Postuma_2015]

prohibited_recommendations: Do not prescribe metoclopramide, prochlorperazine, haloperidol or other centrally acting D2-blocking antiemetics or antipsychotics; if an antipsychotic is needed, use quetiapine or clozapine
Do not start a centrally acting anticholinergic (trihexyphenidyl, benztropine) for the tremor at 67: confusion and memory impairment, and urinary retention with his prostatic hyperplasia
required_recommendations: Diagnose clinically probable PD (MDS 2015): bradykinesia with decrement and right-predominant rest tremor and rigidity, no absolute exclusion, no red flag; olfactory loss on a validated test (UPSIT 22/40, severe microsmia, when tested) is a second supportive criterion and makes it clinically established, otherwise the response to levodopa may add one [Postuma_2015]

Start carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg, half a tablet three times daily with food, increasing over 2 to 4 weeks to one tablet three times daily (300 mg/day levodopa), and review the response after 2 to 3 months, and measure lying and standing blood pressure at each step because tamsulosin and amlodipine add to orthostatic falls [NICE_NG71]
If a dopamine agonist is used, warn about impulse control disorders and excessive daytime sleepiness and ask about them at every visit [NICE_NG71]

Address driving: his wife reports slower reactions and hesitancy at intersections; advise a formal driving assessment, and no driving if sudden sleep onset or excessive daytime sleepiness occurs on dopaminergic treatment [NICE_NG71]
Refer to physiotherapy for gait initiation and turning, occupational therapy for dressing and handwriting, and speech and language therapy for the hypophonia [NICE_NG71]

avoided_actions.rationale: No seizure, episodic confusion or encephalopathy: EEG does not inform this parkinsonism
No inflammatory, infectious or rapidly progressive feature: CSF has no role in this typical parkinsonism
No murmur, heart failure or cardiac symptom: an echocardiogram does not inform the parkinsonism
No syncope, falls or palpitations: rhythm monitoring is not indicated
No cardiac symptom, syncope or QT-relevant drug planned: an ECG does not inform the parkinsonism
DaT SPECT is indicated when tremor cannot be clinically separated from parkinsonism; here the clinical diagnosis is clear and the scan would not change management [NICE_NG71]
Formal autonomic testing is not part of the PD work-up; bedside orthostatic measurement suffices

key_clinical_evidence: Right-predominant bradykinesia with decrement, 4-5 Hz pill-rolling rest tremor with re-emergence, cogwheel rigidity, micrographia, hypophonia and hypomimia: MDS 2015 parkinsonism

Rest tremor is the one supportive criterion before any levodopa trial; the self-reported smell loss is a second only on a validated test (UPSIT 22/40); no red flag and no absolute exclusion: clinically probable PD, clinically established once the smell test confirms the loss

alternatives: Pramipexole or ropinirole (dopamine agonists), titrated gradually; more somnolence, impulse control disorders and hallucinations than levodopa

contraindications: Non-selective MAO inhibitors (phenelzine, tranylcypromine) with levodopa: risk of hypertensive crisis. Not on the current list.
general.formulary_status: On formulary, no prior authorization required
interactions: Tamsulosin (alpha-1 blocker) lowers standing blood pressure and adds to the orthostatic fall; levodopa can lower it further. Review the need for each and measure lying and standing blood pressure at each levodopa dose step.
Amlodipine lowers blood pressure and adds to the same orthostatic effect.
warnings: Acetaminophen: no clinically relevant interaction with levodopa.
Nausea is common at initiation; taking the dose with a small carbohydrate snack helps.
High-protein meals reduce levodopa absorption; if fluctuations develop later, separate doses from protein-rich meals.
Dopaminergic drugs can cause somnolence and sudden sleep onset: counsel about driving.
Impulse control disorders (gambling, hypersexuality, compulsive shopping, binge eating) occur mainly with dopamine agonists.
Vivid dreams or hallucinations can occur, more often in older patients.

patient.history_present_illness:
Mr. Caruso is a 67-year-old right-handed retired engineer who presents to the neurology clinic referred by his primary care physician for evaluation of a progressive right hand tremor and generalized slowing of movements. His wife, who accompanies him, reports that she first noticed a subtle intermittent tremor in his right hand approximately two and a half years ago while he was sitting watching television. The tremor was initially mild and occurred only at rest, but has gradually become more persistent and noticeable, particularly when he is relaxed or distracted. He reports that the tremor temporarily stops when he deliberately reaches for an object but returns once the hand is resting again.

Over the past 18 months, he has noticed progressive difficulty with fine motor tasks on the right side. Buttoning his shirt has become a daily struggle, and his handwriting has become progressively smaller and more difficult to read. His wife has noticed that he takes much longer to get dressed in the morning than he used to. He also reports that his right arm feels stiff and does not swing naturally when he walks, which his wife corroborated, noting that she first observed this change approximately one year ago.

More recently, over the past six to eight months, he has noticed that his gait has changed. He describes taking shorter steps and occasionally feeling as though his feet are momentarily stuck to the floor when he starts walking, though frank freezing episodes have not been described. His wife has noticed that he has developed a slight forward stoop. He has not fallen but has felt unsteady when turning quickly. He reports that his voice has become softer, and his wife often asks him to speak up during conversations. He has also noticed mild constipation over the past year, which he attributes to reduced physical activity, and some difficulty with his sense of smell that he has not previously mentioned to a physician.

He denies any cognitive complaints, hallucinations, or vivid dreams. His wife notes no significant personality changes. He continues to manage household finances and participates in social activities, though she observes he has become somewhat less enthusiastic about going out. His sleep has been generally adequate, and he denies any acting out of dreams or unusual nocturnal movements.

neurological_exam.additional: Glabellar tap: positive (Myerson sign, fails to habituate after 10 taps). Handwriting sample obtained: micrographia noted with progressive diminution of letter size across a written sentence. Seborrhea noted on the forehead and nasolabial folds.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose testing without dysmetria bilaterally, though movements are slow on the right. Heel-to-shin testing intact. Rapid alternating movements markedly slow and decremental on the right, mildly slow on the left.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal, round, and reactive to light bilaterally. Extraocular movements full without nystagmus. Reduced blink frequency noted. Facial expression is hypomimic with masked facies. Facial sensation intact bilaterally. Hearing grossly intact. Palate elevates symmetrically. Sternocleidomastoid and trapezius strength 5/5 bilaterally. Tongue midline without fasciculations.
neurological_exam.gait: Gait notable for reduced right arm swing, mildly shortened stride length, and slight forward-flexed posture. Mild difficulty with initiation of gait. No festination observed. Turns require 4-5 steps (slightly increased). Pull test reveals one step backward recovery (retropulsion mildly positive). Romberg sign negative.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented to person, place, time, and situation. Speech is mildly hypophonic with reduced prosody but no dysarthria. Language fluent without paraphasic errors. Naming, repetition, and comprehension intact. Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score 27/30 (lost 1 point on visuospatial/executive, 1 on delayed recall, 1 on verbal fluency). Affect is mildly flat but appropriately engaged.
neurological_exam.motor: Tone: Cogwheel rigidity at the right wrist and right elbow, with mild rigidity at the left wrist. Strength is 5/5 throughout all extremities. Bradykinesia is prominent in the right upper extremity with reduced amplitude and speed on finger tapping, hand opening/closing, and pronation-supination. Mild bradykinesia in the left upper extremity. Right hand rest tremor at approximately 4-5 Hz, pill-rolling in character, diminishes with action and re-emerges when the hand is at rest in the lap. Mild postural tremor in the right hand. No tremor observed in the left hand or lower extremities.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ and symmetric at biceps, triceps, brachioradialis, patellar, and Achilles tendons bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally. No Hoffmann sign.
neurological_exam.sensory: Light touch, pinprick, proprioception, and vibration intact in all extremities. No cortical sensory deficits.
